correctness.rationale: The complete direction-width support law on z uniform in [0,1] gives the exact radius-normalized first two moment integrals a/2 and b/3. Differentiation yields the positive-factor identity V_prime=8t A(t)(pi-T(t))/(3a(t)^3(1+t^2)^(3/2)). On 0<t<=3 the exact T derivative has numerator sqrt(1+y)P(y)-Q(y), negative by exhaustive P<=0 and P>0 polynomial comparisons. On t>=3 a simple rational bound gives T<pi. Since T diverges as t decreases to zero, exactly one root exists and is global minimum. T(sqrt(3))=pi/3+6sqrt(3)/5<pi proves it precedes the known worst-case minimizer. Checker independently evaluates quadratures, finite arithmetic identities, and numerical roots, not infinite inequalities.

value.rationale: The scale-free relative width variance quantifies mean-square departure from constant width in the most canonical circular-cone similarity family. Its exact unique optimum has coefficient of variation about 4.11%, while a different cone uniquely minimizes worst-case directional spread. This rigorous separation between L2 and L-infinity isotropy, requiring a global nontrivial uniqueness argument, is a meaningful natural-shape classification rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The result supplies an exact benchmark for cone-like shape uniformity; no universal convex-body optimality is claimed.
